QF.id: SIA Social Stock Exchange Introduction and Instruments_14

question.text: Ms. Sunita Patil is assessing two proposed fundraises: (X) Asha Deep Trust plans a ZCZP public issue for a women-empowerment project; (Y) a consortium of three NPOs plans a Development Impact Bond for literacy outcomes across 3 states. The MOST material difference for her impact-assessment approach is:

answer.text: Both are identical in treatment; the SIA applies the same SAS-200 indicators to both.
The ZCZP requires no impact measurement because there is no return; the DIB requires full measurement because it is pay-for-success.

The DIB is outcome-linked (payments released only on verified outcomes against pre-agreed metrics) requiring outcome-verification rigour, while the ZCZP is donation-based (funders expect social impact but payment is upfront and non-returnable), requiring output/outcome tracking but no pay-for-success gating.
The ZCZP is settled on stock exchanges while DIBs are off-market bilateral contracts with no listing possibility.

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Section 2.3.1.2, DIBs are pay-for-success — the outcome funder pays only on verified delivery of pre-agreed metrics, requiring an independent third-party evaluator (the SIA) to gate payments. ZCZPs are donation instruments issued upfront with no payment gating on outcomes; the funder's 'loss' is reputational (future donation flow). This changes the SIA's approach: DIBs demand reasonable-assurance-grade rigour on attribution, while ZCZP assurance typically focuses on output/outcome reporting quality. The Trap: Option A ignores the pay-for-success gating. Option B wrongly claims ZCZPs need no measurement — they do, for the Annual Impact Report. Option D is factually wrong because DIBs CAN be listed on SSE (Section 2.3.1.2 explicitly permits DIB listing on SSE). Cross-Exam Context: XV (Research Analyst) treats outcome-linked bond valuation. XIX-A/B/C/D/E treats AIF structures that can underwrite DIB risk tranches. Assessor's Pro-Tip: For a DIB engagement, draft a separate attribution-testing memo that isolates the NPO's intervention effect from confounding factors (government schemes, seasonal effects) — outcome-gated payments need defensible counterfactual logic; a ZCZP engagement tolerates a lighter attribution narrative.
